newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse slips in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse slips in cautious trade.

text.p: CASABLANCA, July 7 Reuter) - The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Monday 0.02 percent lower with blue-chip stocks stagnating and a few others making small advances in a still cautious market, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 637.87 points from 638.02 points on Friday.
"Blue-chip firms remained unchanged...Only small shareholders buying small quantities are on the market," a broker at Sogebourse said.
Stockbrokers attribute the caution to statements that some of the market's share prices appeared higher than warranted.

Among the few good performers were silver mine Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter which added 17 dirhams to 595 dirhams with 2,473 shares exchanged. Imiter which has been floated on the stock exchange early in June had an initial price of 396 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private group, advanced five dirhams to 725 dirhams.
First and second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued respectively in January and May 1996, rose six and two dirhams to 1,365 and 1,172 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur rose 12 dirhams to 600 dirhams.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir fell six dirhams to 352 dirhams.
Blue-chip Banque Commerciale du Maroc closed unchanged at 860 dirhams.
First Moroccan private conglomerate, ONA Group closed unchanged at 765 dirhams with more than 3,500 shares changing hands.
Steel mill Sonasid was unchanged at 530 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 25 million, up from 24.7 million dirhams on the previous session.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 42 million dirhams, down from 42.9 million. Main trade was in Imiter silver mine with 9,900 shares traded on this market.
